scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Rhythm of the Sparrowhawk
This is Ambasse bey. 20th century.
on_screen: Title card: Ambasse bey · Cameroon · 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Originating among the Yabassi people, the dance was inspired by German court dances during the colonial era.
It gained prominence in Douala post-WWII and served as the foundation for the development of makossa music in the 1960s.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is a cultural expression used to enliven ceremonies.
The opening 'Mudun'a Sombo' sequence is a ritualized act to commune with ancestors and ward off negative forces.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Sawa Traditional Dance(L'Ambass Bey) at a competition.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/21/Sawa_Traditional_Dance%28L%27Ambass_Bey%29_at_a_competition.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform fluid steps and jerky body movements, with a focus on rhythmic shoulder swaying.
The dance begins with the 'Mudun'a Sombo' (old monkey) steps, followed by sequences performed in groups, pairs, or solo.
Instructors provide cues in German.
Watch for Mudun'a Sombo.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is faster than assiko and relies on the guitar, sticks, bottles, and the Conga (Njembe).
It is often sung in the Douala language.
Listen for the guitar, sticks, bottles, Conga (Njembe).
Fast-paced acoustic guitar-driven music with percussive accents from bottles and sticks, creating a rhythmic, driving pulse.

narration: Sallé John (King of Ambasse bey), Eboa Lotin, the Dayas family (Joseph and Engom'a), Tchako, Lobè Ramaud, Belmond M'Packo, and the musician Manulo.
It is a precursor to makossa and shares roots with assiko.
